setup: A circle has radius [[r]] and a central angle of $[[frac]]$.

steps.say: In radians the angle already measures the arc it cuts on a unit circle, so arc length is the radius times the angle: $s = r\theta$. That is the reason arc length is stated in radians — in degrees the formula would carry a factor of $\pi/180$.
Here $s = [[r]] \times [[frac]] = [[value]]\pi$, so the arc length is $[[value]]\pi$ and the multiplier written in front of $\pi$ is [[value]].
